title: Nursing Home Effort Linked to Inspection Cycle
discussion_signal: The NBER announcement frames inspections as a timing and incentive problem: nursing-home effort fluctuates with the inspection cycle, while unpredictable inspections may increase effort and save lives. The public signal shifts attention from whether inspection exists to whether providers can anticipate and temporarily adapt to it.
linked_research_question: Which inspection designs produce durable quality rather than temporary compliance, and how do ratings, mortality, staffing, and provider adaptation interact for residents and public payers?
limits: The announcement is a short research translation and does not provide the full estimates
Inspection response is not the same as durable quality or resident welfare
Public discussion cannot establish provider prevalence or the effect of alternative inspection designs
